title: Articles a / an / the
objectives: Use a before consonant sounds and an before vowel sounds.
Understand basic use of the for specific things.
Choose a/an/the correctly in common phrases.
canDo: I can use a, an, and the in common noun phrases.

warmUp.title: Artigos
warmUp.prompt: Português tem "um/uma" e "o/a". Inglês usa a/an e the. When do you think we use each?

explanation:
Indefinite articles: a + consonant sound (a book, a university /ju/) | an + vowel sound (an apple, an hour /au/)

Use a/an for one non-specific thing: I am a student. She is an engineer.

Definite article the = specific: The book on the table is mine.

Jobs/nationalities: He is a doctor. She is an Brazilian? ✗ → She is Brazilian. (no article with nationality adjectives)

grammar.title: Articles a / an / the
grammar.rule: Use a/an for singular countable nouns mentioned for the first time or as examples. Use the when the listener knows which one. No article with plural generics in general statements.

examples.sentence: The pen on the desk is blue.

sentences: I have a dog. The dog is friendly.
He is a teacher at a big school.

reading.title: A Day at the Market
reading.text: Paula goes to the market. She buys an apple, a loaf of bread, and a bottle of water. The apple is green. The bread is fresh. At home, she puts the apple in a bowl. The bowl is on the table.

questions.question: What does Paula buy first in the list?
Where is the bowl?
questions.explanation: The bowl is on the table.

writing.prompt: Write 5 sentences about things in your room. Use a/an/the at least once each.
writing.modelAnswer: I have a bed and a desk. The desk is small. There is an lamp on the desk. The lamp is white. I like the chair — it is comfortable.

tutorHints: Teach sound not spelling: a university, an hour.
